JOIN ds_demographics_census_regions r ON h.region_id = r.region_id
GROUP BY r.state
ORDER BY r.state;

       COUNT(*) AS total_individuals,

sql:
WITH household_income AS (
  SELECT i.household_id, SUM(i.income) AS total_income
  FROM ds_demographics_census_individuals i
  GROUP BY i.household_id
)
SELECT r.name AS region_name, AVG(hi.total_income) AS avg_household_income
FROM ds_demographics_census_regions r
JOIN ds_demographics_census_households h ON r.region_id = h.region_id
JOIN household_income hi ON h.household_id = hi.household_id
GROUP BY r.name
ORDER BY avg_household_income DESC;

sql:
WITH household_income AS (
  SELECT
    r.state,
    h.area_type,
    h.household_id,
    SUM(i.income) AS income
  FROM ds_demographics_census_households h
  JOIN ds_demographics_census_individuals i ON i.household_id = h.household_id
  JOIN ds_demographics_census_regions r ON r.region_id = h.region_id
  WHERE h.area_type IN ('Urban', 'Rural')
  GROUP BY r.state, h.area_type, h.household_id
)
SELECT
  state,
  ROUND(AVG(income) FILTER (WHERE area_type = 'Urban'), 2) AS avg_urban_household_income,
  ROUND(AVG(income) FILTER (WHERE area_type = 'Rural'), 2) AS avg_rural_household_income,
  ROUND(
    AVG(income) FILTER (WHERE area_type = 'Urban') -
    AVG(income) FILTER (WHERE area_type = 'Rural'), 2
  ) AS income_gap
FROM household_income
WHERE area_type IN ('Urban', 'Rural')
GROUP BY state
ORDER BY income_gap DESC NULLS LAST;
question: What is the income gap between urban and rural households, by state?

sql: WITH education_totals AS (SELECT education, COUNT(*) AS total, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE employment IN ('Employed', 'Self-Employed')) AS employed FROM ds_demographics_census_individuals GROUP BY education), education_region AS (SELECT i.education, r.name AS region, COUNT(*) AS total, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE i.employment IN ('Employed', 'Self-Employed')) AS employed FROM ds_demographics_census_individuals i JOIN ds_demographics_census_households h ON i.household_id = h.household_id JOIN ds_demographics_census_regions r ON h.region_id = r.region_id GROUP BY i.education, r.name) SELECT er.education, er.region, er.employed * 100.0 / er.total AS employment_rate_pct, et.employed * 100.0 / et.total AS overall_employment_rate_pct FROM education_region er JOIN education_totals et ON er.education = et.education ORDER BY overall_employment_rate_pct DESC, er.region;

sql: WITH income_bands AS (SELECT percentile_cont(0.9) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY income) AS p90, percentile_cont(0.1) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY income) AS p10 FROM ds_demographics_census_individuals), classified AS (SELECT i.individual_id, i.income, h.region_id, r.name AS region_name, CASE WHEN i.income >= b.p90 THEN 'Top Decile' WHEN i.income <= b.p10 THEN 'Bottom Decile' ELSE 'Middle 80%' END AS income_group FROM ds_demographics_census_individuals i JOIN ds_demographics_census_households h ON i.household_id = h.household_id JOIN ds_demographics_census_regions r ON h.region_id = r.region_id CROSS JOIN income_bands b) SELECT region_name, income_group, COUNT(*) AS individual_count FROM classified WHERE income_group IN ('Top Decile', 'Bottom Decile') GROUP BY region_name, income_group ORDER BY region_name, income_group;
